docs.title: Current KYC Management Application
docs.text: Document Type: Business Overview Audience: Compliance Team, Management, Business Stakeholders System: Existing JSF Web Application Status: Live Production System

docs.title: What Is This System?
docs.text:
The KYC Management Application is Qatari Diar's internal web-based system for managing Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence reports. It replaces paper files and email chains with a digital record of every counterparty screened by the Enterprise Risk & Compliance team.

A counterparty is any person or company that Qatari Diar plans to do business with — a supplier, buyer, tenant, contractor, investor, or joint venture partner.

Before QD enters into a significant business relationship, the compliance team must research the counterparty, verify their identity, assess any risks, and obtain management approval. This system manages that process from start to finish.

docs.title: Who Uses It?
docs.text: Role What They Do in the System Contributor Compliance officer who creates and submits KYC reports Level 1 Approver Reviews and approves reports for low-risk cases; first reviewer for medium/high risk Level 2 / RFI Approver Final sign-off for medium and high-risk cases; handles information requests Administrator Manages users, reference data, and system configuration

docs.title: 1. Manages Counterparty Records (Entities)
docs.text:
Before creating a KYC report, the compliance team records information about the counterparty in the system. This is called an Entity.

For a natural person (an individual), the system captures: - Full name, nationality, date of birth - ID or passport number - Screening results from international databases

For a legal entity (a company), the system captures: - Company name, registration number, headquarters - Ownership structure - Details of the people who ultimately own or control the company — these are called Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs)

Each UBO's identity is recorded individually, including their nationality, ID number, and the results of screening them through international databases.

docs.title: 2. Creates and Manages KYC Reports
docs.text:
A KYC report is the formal compliance document that records everything the team has found about a counterparty and what decision was reached.

Each report includes: - Which company or person was investigated - What type of relationship QD plans to have with them - What level of due diligence was applied (Simplified, Standard, or Enhanced) - What the screening found - The compliance officer's conclusion and recommendation - The assessed risk level (Low, Medium, or High) - Supporting documents

docs.title: 3. Routes Reports Through an Approval Process
docs.text:
Once a compliance officer completes a report, it goes through a formal approval process before it is finalised.

flowchart TD
    CO([Compliance Officer\nCreates Report]) --> SUBMIT[Submits for Approval]
    SUBMIT --> L1[Level 1 Approver\nReviews]
    L1 --> A1{Decision}
    A1 -->|Approve — Low Risk| FINAL([✅ Final Approval])
    A1 -->|Request More Info| RFI[Report returned\nto Officer with comment]
    A1 -->|Reject| REJ1([❌ Closed])
    RFI --> RESUBMIT[Officer responds\nand resubmits]
    RESUBMIT --> L1
    A1 -->|Approve — Medium/High Risk| L2[Level 2 Approver\nReviews]
    L2 --> A2{Decision}
    A2 -->|Final Approve| FINAL
    A2 -->|Request More Info| RFI
    A2 -->|Reject| REJ2([❌ Closed])

    style FINAL fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style REJ1 fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style REJ2 fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style RFI fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100

Important rule: A report cannot be approved by the same person who created it. Low-risk reports require one approval signature. Medium and high-risk reports require two separate approvals.

docs.title: 4. Tracks Everything with a Full Audit Trail
docs.text: Every action taken — every submission, approval, rejection, or request for information — is permanently recorded with the date, time, and the name of the person who took the action. This audit trail cannot be edited or deleted.

docs.title: 5. Stores Supporting Documents
docs.text: The system holds all documents submitted as evidence: commercial registrations, identity documents, shareholder certificates, and any other supporting material. These documents are linked directly to the KYC report they support.

docs.title: 6. Generates PDF Reports
docs.text: The system can produce a formal PDF version of any KYC report. Unfinished reports are watermarked as "Draft" to prevent them from being used as official documents.

docs.title: 7. Provides Search and Filtering
docs.text: The compliance team can search the full history of KYC reports by: - Reference number - Counterparty name - Risk level (Low / Medium / High) - Approval status - Report status - The officer who conducted the due diligence

docs.title: How a KYC Report Moves Through the System
Step-by-Step
docs.text:
Step 1 — Create the Entity The compliance officer creates a record for the counterparty, entering their details and the results of searching them against international screening databases (WorldCheck and others).

Step 2 — Add UBOs (if a company) If the counterparty is a company, the officer records each significant owner or authorised signatory — including their screening results.

Step 3 — Create the KYC Report The officer creates the formal report, linking it to the entity, classifying the type of due diligence, recording the findings and conclusion, setting the risk level, and attaching supporting documents.

Step 4 — Save as Draft or Submit The officer can save a draft to complete later, or submit the finished report for approval.

Step 5 — Level 1 Review The appointed Level 1 Approver reviews the full report, including all documents. They can approve it, send it back with questions, or reject it.

Step 6 — Level 2 Review (Medium/High Risk) For anything above low risk, a second senior approver independently reviews and makes the final decision.

Step 7 — Completion Once fully approved, the report is finalised and archived. A PDF can be generated and sent to the team that originally requested the KYC.

docs.title: Reference Data the System Manages
docs.text:
The system uses configurable reference tables that administrators can update without changing the software:

  • Business Counterparty Categories — e.g., Supplier, Buyer, Investor, Tenant
  • Report Statuses — with colour codes for quick visual identification
  • Screening Results — categories for what the international databases returned
  • Request Originators — the teams or individuals who requested KYC checks

docs.title: What the System Does Not Currently Do
docs.text:
Being transparent about current limitations helps set expectations:

Limitation Impact No automatic notification to the original requester when a report is approved Requesters must be informed manually No live KPI dashboard — metrics require a manual data export Management reporting is slow and labour-intensive No scheduled reminders for periodic KYC reviews Overdue reviews are not flagged automatically No digital intake from requesting departments — requests arrive by email Inconsistent formats, no tracking Passwords are not strongly secured Security risk that should be addressed

These limitations are addressed in Version 3 (Best Practice) and Version 4 (APEX Implementation).

docs.title: How We Work Today: The As-Is KYC Process
docs.text:
Document Type: Business Process Guide Audience: Compliance Team, Management Source: Requirements Gathering Session — Head of Enterprise Risk & Compliance Status: Current manual process — basis for all future improvements

This document faithfully captures how the compliance team currently operates — including every manual step, every tool used, and every known difficulty. It is not a criticism; it is an honest baseline from which to improve.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Today, the KYC process at Qatari Diar is a mostly manual process. The existing KYC Report Application (a JSF-based web system) is used only at the end: the officer enters the completed report data and the system manages the approval workflow and record storage. Everything before that — receiving requests, collecting documents, conducting due diligence, and compiling the full report — is done entirely outside the system through email, Excel, WorldCheck, and personal judgment. The system never sees the work; it only sees the finished output.

This creates real risks: inconsistency between departments, reliance on personal memory, difficulty onboarding new staff, and no reliable way to answer basic management questions like "how many KYC reports did we complete this quarter?" without first requesting a data export.

docs.title: Phase 0: Deciding Whether a KYC is Needed
docs.text:
Who does this: The business department that wants to engage a new counterparty

Before the compliance team is even involved, the requesting department runs a check using an Excel-based Risk Calculator. This spreadsheet was built to match QD's internal KYC policy and asks a series of questions about the counterparty:

  • Who are they? (a company or an individual)
  • Where are they from? (Qatari, majority-Qatari, minority-Qatari, foreign)
  • What type of relationship does QD plan to have with them? (supplier, buyer, tenant, investor, etc.)
  • Is there any financial involvement, current or proposed?
  • Are there any known connections to related parties?

Based on the answers, the Excel says either "KYC Required" or "KYC Not Required".

flowchart TD
    EXCEL([Department fills in\nExcel Risk Calculator]) --> Q{KYC Required?}
    Q -->|YES| DOCS[Department gathers documents\nand sends email to\ncompliance mailbox]
    Q -->|NO| LOCAL[Excel output saved locally\nas evidence\nNo document collection required]

    style DOCS fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style LOCAL fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style EXCEL fill:#F3E5F5,color:#4A148C,stroke:#6A1B9A

What goes wrong here

  • No formal evidence record when KYC is not required — just files on someone's laptop
  • The Excel can be manually changed — output depends on the person filling it in
  • Requests arrive in different formats from different departments — no standard

What goes wrong here: - Different departments send requests in completely different formats — there is no standard - When KYC is not required, the supporting documents are saved locally but there is no formal evidence record that the check was done - The Excel can be changed manually, so the output depends on the honesty and judgment of the person filling it in

docs.title: Phase 1: Receiving and Validating Documents
docs.text:
Who does this: Compliance Officer

The compliance team receives an email in their shared mailbox. The email contains the Risk Calculator and attached documents. The officer opens everything and checks whether the documentation is sufficient to conduct proper due diligence.

What "sufficient" means:

For an individual person: A government-issued photo ID (Qatar ID or passport) is generally enough.

For a company: The officer needs an official document that shows — clearly and completely — who owns the company and who controls it. In Qatar, a Commercial Registration (CR) usually does this. In other countries (Egypt, UK, Tajikistan), different documents serve this purpose — so there is no single fixed checklist.

What the officer is always looking for is: "Can I trace the ownership all the way to a real person?"

flowchart TD
    RECV([Documents Received\nvia Email]) --> CHECK{Sufficient?}
    CHECK -->|NO| REQ[Request more documents\nby email to department]
    REQ --> REPLY[Department replies\nby email]
    REPLY --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|YES| SAVE[Save documents to\nlocal folder on workstation]
    SAVE --> SIGNAL[Signal to manager\nverbally or by email:\n'Ready for assignment']

    style RECV fill:#E3F2FD,color:#0D47A1,stroke:#1565C0
    style SAVE fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style REQ fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C

What goes wrong here: - Everything is tracked in email threads — there is no system record of how many rounds of back-and-forth happened - Documents are saved to the officer's local workstation. At the end of the day, they must be manually moved to a QDocs folder — but there is no check for whether a folder for that entity already exists, and no standard naming convention - New staff (e.g., Hessa) have no way to know if a report has been done before for the same entity. Institutional knowledge lives only in people's memories

docs.title: Phase 2: Assigning the Work
docs.text:
Who does this: Compliance Manager

The manager looks at who is available (not on leave, not overloaded) and assigns the case to a compliance officer. This is done verbally or by email — there is no assignment record in the system.

What goes wrong here: - Assignment happens outside the system — there is no record of when or to whom a case was assigned - The manager has no workload view; they must ask each officer individually how many active cases they have - If the manager is absent, there is no way for the team to know how work should be prioritised or distributed

docs.title: Phase 3: Conducting the Due Diligence (WorldCheck)
docs.text:
Who does this: Compliance Officer

Once assigned, the officer opens WorldCheck — an external international database — in their web browser. This is a separate tool, entirely disconnected from the KYC system.

For each entity and each significant individual (UBO), the officer: 1. Searches by name 2. Reviews the results for matches 3. Determines whether a match is genuine or a false positive 4. Notes whether the entity or person is a PEP (Politically Exposed Person) — for example, a state-owned company is connected to the government, which counts as a PEP link 5. Looks at shareholders and connected entities

flowchart TD
    WC([Open WorldCheck\nin browser]) --> SEARCH[Search entity / person by name]
    SEARCH --> MATCH{Review matches}
    MATCH --> M1[Direct match?\nGenuine or false positive?]
    MATCH --> M2[PEP connection?]
    MATCH --> M3[Adverse findings?]
    MATCH --> M4[Check shareholders]
    M1 & M2 & M3 & M4 --> JUDGE[Apply risk-based judgement:\nHow deep do I need to go?]
    JUDGE --> EX1[Simple case e.g. Microsoft Qatar\n→ Stop at Qatar entity level]
    JUDGE --> EX2[Complex unknown structure\n→ Go deeper where risk justifies it]
    EX1 & EX2 --> NOTE[Note findings manually\nin memory or personal document]
    NOTE --> SYSTEM[Enter findings later\ninto KYC system free-text field]

    style WC fill:#F3E5F5,color:#4A148C,stroke:#6A1B9A
    style NOTE fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style SYSTEM fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB

What goes wrong here: - There is no structured way to record what was found — it goes into a free-text field in the system later - There is no record of when the screening was done or which databases were checked - The officer carries the findings in their head until they sit down to enter them into the system

docs.title: Phase 4: Recording the Entity in the System
docs.text:
Who does this: Compliance Officer

The officer logs into the KYC system and creates an Entity record for the counterparty, entering all the details from their research. For companies, they add each UBO and authorised signatory as a separate sub-record.

What goes wrong here: - The system does not check whether this entity was already recorded before. If the same company was screened six months ago, the officer won't know unless they remember or happen to search - Screening results go into a single free-text box — there is no structure for recording the date, the source, whether it was a match or not, or whether the person is a PEP - Date fields (like date of birth) accept any text — the system will happily accept "12-0-2024" or "32/13/2025" without warning

docs.title: Phase 5: Creating the KYC Report
docs.text:
Who does this: Compliance Officer

Next, the officer creates the formal KYC report in the system. This involves entering many fields that could theoretically be pre-filled from the entity record — but the system requires re-entering them from scratch.

One particular pain point: the final conclusion. Around 95% of the time, the conclusion follows a standard template. But those templates are stored in Word documents on shared drives, not in the system. The officer opens Word, copies the relevant template, pastes it into the system, and adjusts it.

flowchart TD
    NEW([Create new KYC report
in system]) --> LINK[Link to entity
no auto-population
re-enter all fields manually]
    LINK --> CLASS[Enter classification:
Simplified / AdHoc / Enhanced
Who requested it and when
Risk level: Low / Medium / High]
    CLASS --> CONC[Write conclusion:
Open Word document
Copy template
Paste into system
Adjust manually]
    CONC --> UPLOAD[Upload documents
from local folder on workstation]
    UPLOAD --> ACTION{Choose action}
    ACTION -->|Save Draft| DRAFT[Stays in officer's queue
for later]
    ACTION -->|Submit for Approval| APPROVER[Goes to approver's queue]

    style NEW fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style CONC fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style APPROVER fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32

What goes wrong here: - The request date field has no validation — an officer under pressure might inadvertently enter a wrong year and not notice - The system does not warn when the entered date does not match the actual chronology of events - Documents must be uploaded from the local workstation — they cannot be linked from QDocs

docs.title: Phase 6: Level 1 Approval
docs.text:
Who does this: Level 1 Approver (currently Latifa)

Where this happens: Inside the KYC Report Application (the existing JSF system). The approver logs into the application and sees the submitted report in their approval queue.

The approver reviews the full report, reads the conclusion, checks the attached documents, and then acts directly in the application:

  • Approve — satisfied with the work; status moves to Approved (L1)
  • Request For Information (RFI) — something is unclear; sends the report back to the officer with a comment recorded in the application
  • Reject — the report is closed with a stated reason recorded in the application

Approval routing by risk (handled by the application): - Low risk → Level 1 approval is the final approval — report status moves to Final Approved - Medium or High risk → report automatically routes to Level 2 queue

flowchart TD
    QUEUE([Report appears in\nL1 Approver's queue\nin KYC Report Application]) --> REVIEW[Approver reviews report\nconclusion + documents\nin the application]
    REVIEW --> DECISION{Decision}
    DECISION -->|Approve| RISK{Risk Level?}
    DECISION -->|RFI| BACK[Report returned to officer\nwith comment — in application]
    DECISION -->|Reject| REJECT([Report closed\nReason recorded in application])

    RISK -->|Low Risk| FINAL([Final Approved\nin application])
    RISK -->|Medium / High Risk| L2([Routes to L2 queue\nin application])

    style QUEUE fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style FINAL fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style REJECT fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style BACK fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100
    style L2 fill:#F3E5F5,color:#4A148C,stroke:#6A1B9A

What goes wrong here: - If the Level 1 Approver is unavailable (on leave, travel), a substitute must be manually arranged by phone or email — the system has no delegation mechanism - There is no way in the system to see how many reports are waiting for approval at any given time

docs.title: Phase 7: Level 2 Approval (Medium/High Risk Only)
docs.text:
Who does this: Level 2 Approver / Head of Compliance (Carlos)

Where this happens: Inside the KYC Report Application — the report appears in Carlos's queue after L1 approval.

Same actions as Level 1 — full review inside the application, then Approve / RFI / Reject. Once approved at Level 2, the report status is set to Final Approved in the application.

flowchart TD
    L2Q([Report appears in\nL2 Approver's queue\nin KYC Report Application]) --> REVIEW2[Approver reviews report\nin the application]
    REVIEW2 --> DECISION2{Decision}
    DECISION2 -->|Approve| FINAL2([Final Approved\nin application])
    DECISION2 -->|RFI| BACK2[Report returned to officer\nwith comment — in application]
    DECISION2 -->|Reject| REJECT2([Report closed\nReason recorded in application])

    style L2Q fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style FINAL2 fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style REJECT2 fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style BACK2 fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100

What goes wrong here: - If the Level 2 Approver (Carlos) is unavailable, a substitute must be manually activated by phone — the system has no delegation or deputy mechanism - There is no mandatory checkpoint for Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) — the question of whether a SAR should be filed is not formally built into the approval step

What should happen but doesn't: The requesting department should automatically receive the completed report and a notification that the KYC is done. Currently, this does not happen — someone on the compliance team has to remember to email them.

docs.title: Phase 8: Reporting and Tracking
docs.text:
Current reality:

There is no live dashboard. When management needs to know: - How many KYCs were completed this month? - How long is our average turnaround time? - Which cases are overdue?

The answer is always: "Madi, send me an export." A data extract is requested, downloaded to Excel, and manually analysed.

Additionally, there is no system to flag when a previously approved KYC is due for periodic review. This is managed — imperfectly — by memory and the manager's judgment.

docs.title: Process Status Labels (Current)
docs.text:
The compliance team informally categorises their pipeline using these statuses — some are in the system, some exist only in email folder labels:

Status Where It Lives Meaning In Progress Email / memory Officer actively working on it Waiting for More Information Email flag Documents requested from department Waiting for Approval KYC System Report submitted, in approver's queue Draft KYC System Saved but not yet submitted Submitted KYC System Sent to Level 1 Approved (L1) KYC System Passed Level 1 review Approved (Final) KYC System All approvals complete Rejected KYC System Closed — not proceeding RFI KYC System Information requested by approver

docs.title: 5. Acceptance Criteria (for As-Is Functionality)
docs.text:
Each of the following must pass before a replacement system is considered functionally equivalent to the current one:

AC-01: A compliance officer can create an entity (natural person or legal entity)
       with all required fields and at least one UBO record.

AC-02: A compliance officer can create a KYC report, link it to an entity,
       upload at least one document, and submit it for approval.

AC-03: A Level 1 approver can view the submitted report (including documents),
       add a comment, and take one of three actions: Approve, RFI, Reject.

AC-04: When an RFI is issued, the contributor receives notification,
       can view the comment, and can resubmit the updated report.

AC-05: For a medium or high-risk report, Level 1 approval routes it
       to the Level 2 queue — not directly to final approval.

AC-06: All approval actions are recorded in ProcessLog with:
       timestamp, user, action type, and comment.

AC-07: A PDF can be generated for any KYC report.
       Draft reports are watermarked "Draft".
       Approved reports have no draft watermark.

AC-08: A user with Contributor role cannot access the approval queue pages.
       A user with Approver role cannot create or edit KYC reports.

AC-09: Reference data (BCP categories, statuses, results, request-by list)
       can be added, edited, and deactivated by an Admin user.

AC-10: Session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.
       User is redirected to the login page.

docs.title: Best Practice KYC Process
docs.text: Document Type: Business Process Guide Audience: Compliance Team, Management, Internal Auditors, Regulators Standards: FATF 40 Recommendations | Basel KYC | EU 6AMLD | ISO 31000 Status: Target operating model — design for next-generation system

docs.title: Why This Redesign?
docs.text:
The requirements gathering session identified that the current process relies too heavily on individual memory, email threads, and personal judgment. This creates inconsistency, audit gaps, and significant operational risk.

This redesigned process achieves four things: 1. Replaces manual steps with system-enforced controls wherever the decision is rule-based 2. Preserves human judgment for the steps that genuinely require expertise 3. Creates a complete evidence trail that satisfies regulatory examination 4. Gives management visibility without needing to request data extracts

docs.title: The Seven Principles This Process Upholds
docs.text:
Every step in this process is designed around seven core compliance principles:

  1. Know Who You Are Dealing With — Identity verified, ownership traced
  2. Assess the Risk — Risk level determined systematically, not just by feel
  3. Match the Effort to the Risk — More scrutiny for higher-risk counterparties
  4. Two Pairs of Eyes — No single person approves their own work
  5. Leave a Trail — Every action documented, timestamped, and attributable
  6. Protect the Evidence — Documents stored properly, not on someone's laptop
  7. Keep It Current — KYCs reviewed regularly, not just once

docs.title: The Improved Process: Phase by Phase
Phase 0: Standardised Digital Intake
docs.text:
What changes: Business departments no longer send emails in any format they like. Instead, they complete a structured digital intake form in the system.

How it works:

flowchart TD
    DEPT([Business Department\nOpens KYC Request Portal]) --> AUTOFILL[Name & department\nauto-filled from Oracle Fusion HCM]
    AUTOFILL --> FORM[Fills in structured form:\nCounterparty name, type, country\nRelationship type\nFinancial involvement\nRelated party declaration]
    FORM --> RULES{System Rules Engine\nCalculates automatically}
    RULES -->|KYC Not Required| WAIVER[Waiver record created\nDocuments stored as evidence\nConfirmation sent to dept]
    RULES -->|KYC Required| CHECKLIST[System shows document checklist\nbased on entity type and country]
    CHECKLIST --> UPLOAD[Department uploads documents\ndirectly in portal — no email]
    UPLOAD --> SUBMIT[Submit]
    SUBMIT --> CASE[Case created: INTAKE-YYYY-NNNNNN\nCompliance team notified automatically]

    style WAIVER fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style CASE fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style DEPT fill:#E3F2FD,color:#0D47A1,stroke:#1565C0

What this fixes: - Every request is in the same format, regardless of which department sends it - When KYC is not required, there is a permanent evidence record — not just a forgotten email - The documents are attached to the case from the very beginning — no local folders

docs.title: Phase 1: Document Validation — System-Assisted
docs.text:
What changes: The compliance team uses a structured checklist rather than relying on experience and memory. The system tracks how many rounds of document requests happen.

flowchart TD
    REVIEW([Compliance Officer\nReviews Submitted Documents]) --> CHECK{Documents meet\nchecklist?}
    CHECK -->|No — Missing or unclear| REQ[Send structured request to department\nSelect document type\nSet deadline\nSystem sends notification automatically]
    REQ --> UPLOAD[Department uploads via portal\nnot by email\nAll rounds tracked with timestamps]
    UPLOAD --> CHECK
    CHECK -->|Yes — All complete| CONFIRM[Officer marks:\nDocuments Complete ✅]
    CONFIRM --> KPI[System records docs_complete_date\n🕐 KPI Clock Starts Here]

    style KPI fill:#F3E5F5,color:#4A148C,stroke:#6A1B9A
    style CONFIRM fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style REQ fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100

The KPI start point is the moment the compliance team confirms they have everything they need. Turnaround time is measured from here — not from the first email the department sent — because the compliance team cannot be held accountable for the department's delay in providing documents.

Duplicate check: When the officer is about to create an entity, the system automatically searches for similar names. If the same company was screened before, the officer is shown the previous record and can choose to link to it, rather than creating a duplicate.

docs.title: Phase 2: Risk Pre-Assessment
docs.text:
What is new: Before the compliance officer begins their research, the system shows them a risk indicator panel — a summary of automated risk signals computed from the data already provided.

flowchart LR
    SYS([System Pre-Computes\nRisk Signals]) --> G[🌍 Geographic Risk\nFATF country tier]
    SYS --> E[🏢 Entity Type Risk\nState-owned = PEP-linked]
    SYS --> S[🔗 Structure Risk\nMultiple ownership layers]
    SYS --> H[⚠️ Historical Flags\nPrior adverse findings]
    G & E & S & H --> SUGGEST[System Suggests\nLOW / MEDIUM / HIGH]
    SUGGEST --> OFFICER{Officer\nAgrees?}
    OFFICER -->|Yes| CONFIRM[Confirm risk level\nand proceed]
    OFFICER -->|No| OVERRIDE[Override risk level\nDocument reason — mandatory]

    style SUGGEST fill:#E8EAF6,color:#1A237E,stroke:#3949AB
    style OVERRIDE fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100
    style CONFIRM fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32

This does not replace the officer's judgment — it gives them a structured starting point and ensures that obvious risk factors are never overlooked.

Risk determines the path: - Low risk → Simplified Due Diligence (one approval required) - Medium risk → Standard KYC (two approvals required) - High risk → Enhanced Due Diligence (two approvals + mandatory additional fields)

docs.title: Phase 3: Due Diligence Research — Structured Evidence Recording
docs.text:
What changes: The screening itself continues to be conducted manually using WorldCheck (or equivalent databases). The change is in how results are recorded in the system.

Instead of a free-text box, the officer completes structured fields for each entity and each UBO:

What is recorded Example Date screening was performed 15 June 2025 Which database(s) were checked WorldCheck (Refinitiv) Reference number from screening tool WC-2025-123456 Match status Potential Match / No Match / Confirmed Match / False Positive PEP flag Yes / No Adverse media flag Yes / No Findings narrative Free text — what was found Resolution note If false positive: why it was dismissed

Why this matters: If a regulator asks "when did you last screen ABC Company, and what did you find?", the answer is in the record — not in someone's email archive.

Escalation rule: If a confirmed match or PEP flag is recorded, the system automatically activates Enhanced Due Diligence requirements, regardless of what was initially selected.

docs.title: Phase 4 & 5: Entity and Report Creation — No Duplicate Entry
docs.text:
What changes: When the officer creates a KYC report after creating the entity, the system automatically copies across the data that was already entered. The officer verifies and enriches — they do not retype.

New mandatory fields for Enhanced KYC: - Source of funds — where does the counterparty's money come from? - Source of wealth — how did they accumulate their assets?

These are required by international standards for high-risk counterparties and cannot be skipped when Enhanced KYC is selected.

Conclusion templates in the system: Standard conclusion texts are stored in the system by risk category. The officer selects the appropriate template, which appears pre-filled in the conclusion field, ready to be personalised. No more opening Word documents.

Date validation: The system will not accept: - Future dates in any date field - Invalid day/month combinations (no 32nd of the 13th month) - Request dates more than 2 years in the past (flags a warning)

SLA indicator: Every report shows a traffic-light indicator: how many days have elapsed versus the target completion time for that report type.

KYC Type Target Completion Simplified 5 business days Standard 10 business days Enhanced 20 business days

docs.title: Phase 6: Level 1 Approval — With Delegation
docs.text:
What changes:

  1. Delegation is pre-configured, not ad-hoc. If the Level 1 Approver marks themselves as on leave, the system automatically routes new submissions to their designated deputy — no phone calls needed.

  2. Structured screening results are visible to the approver in a clear format — not buried in a free-text narrative.

  3. SLA indicator shows the approver if a report is approaching or past its target completion time.

The three approval actions remain the same: Approve / Request For Information / Reject.

For RFI, the approver selects a category (Missing Document / Unclear Conclusion / Insufficient Screening / Other) before entering their comment. This helps analyse why RFIs are happening and whether they can be prevented.

docs.title: Phase 7: Level 2 / MLRO Approval — With SAR Gate
docs.text:
What is new: Before the Level 2 Approver makes their decision, the system asks one additional question:

"Based on your review of this report, is there any information that may require a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)?"

This is a mandatory step. If the answer is yes, the approval is paused and the Head of Compliance is alerted. The SAR process runs separately. If the answer is no, the approval proceeds normally.

This gate ensures that the compliance head consciously considers their SAR obligation on every high-risk case — it cannot be overlooked.

docs.title: Phase 8: Completion — Automated and Monitored
docs.text:
What changes:

On final approval: - The system automatically generates the completed KYC report as a PDF - The requesting department receives an email with the report attached — no manual follow-up needed - The record is sealed (read-only) - A next review date is set automatically based on risk level

Ongoing monitoring: - 60 days before a KYC is due for review: compliance officer notified - On the review date (if not yet renewed): manager notified - SLA breaches on open reports: flagged to manager daily

Live KPI Dashboard — replaces "Madi, send me an export":

The dashboard shows in real time: - Total KYCs completed this month / quarter / year - Average turnaround time - SLA compliance rate - Reports by risk level - Reports by contributor (team productivity) - Pending pipeline (what is in each stage right now) - Overdue cases

docs.text: Document Type: System Requirements Specification (SRS) Audience: Developers, Solution Architects, QA Engineers Standards Applied: FATF 40 | Basel KYC | EU 6AMLD | ISO 31000 Purpose: Complete functional and non-functional requirements for the improved system

docs.title: 1. System Context
docs.text:
The improved KYC system replaces the current JSF application and the surrounding manual processes (Excel, email, local folders). It is a web-based application serving three distinct user groups:

  • Requestors — any Qatari Diar employee who needs a KYC performed
  • Compliance Team — the team that conducts research, creates entities and reports
  • Management — senior officers who approve and have oversight visibility

Decision Logic (initial rules set):

KYC Required = YES if ANY of:

  relationship_type IN (INVESTOR, JV_PARTNER)

docs.title: 5. Acceptance Criteria (V3 additions over V2)
docs.text:
AC-V3-01: KYC necessity engine correctly classifies all 6 ownership categories
          and all configured relationship types. Rules produce consistent output.

AC-V3-02: Intake portal accessible to non-compliance staff.
          Requestor cannot access the full KYC management system.
          Requestor can only see their own submissions.

AC-V3-03: Duplicate detection fires on entity name entry.
          When registration number matches, a warning is mandatory (cannot bypass).

AC-V3-04: Structured screening fields mandatory — "match_status" cannot be NULL
          before report submission.

AC-V3-05: PEP = Y on any entity or UBO automatically triggers ENHANCED KYC.
          SIMPLIFIED type is unavailable in this scenario.

AC-V3-06: ENHANCED KYC: source_of_funds and source_of_wealth are mandatory.
          System blocks submission without these.

AC-V3-07: Delegation active: if approver marked on-leave, their tasks
          automatically route to the configured deputy.

AC-V3-08: SAR gate: L2 approver cannot complete final approval without
          answering the SAR question (Y/N).

AC-V3-09: Final approval: PDF auto-generated and email sent to requestor
          within 60 seconds of approval action.

AC-V3-10: Review schedule: next_review_date = approval_date + N months
          (12 for HIGH, 24 for MEDIUM, 36 for LOW).

AC-V3-11: KPI dashboard shows real-time counts without requiring data export.
          Counts must match direct table query results.

AC-V3-12: Process Log trigger blocks UPDATE and DELETE operations.
          Attempting either returns an error.

AC-V3-13: Date validation blocks future dates in all date fields.
          Invalid dates (e.g., Feb 31) return a validation error.

docs.title: Oracle APEX KYC System
docs.text: Document Type: Business User Guide Audience: All system users — Requestors, Contributors, Approvers, Administrators Platform: Oracle APEX — accessible from any web browser Login: Your existing Oracle Fusion / company network credentials

docs.title: Welcome to the New KYC System
docs.text:
The new KYC system is built on Oracle APEX and is fully connected to the company's Oracle Fusion system. This means:

  • No new username or password. You log in with the same credentials you use for Oracle Fusion.
  • Your details are already in the system. Your name, department, and email come directly from your Fusion employee record.
  • Your role is set automatically. Based on your job role in Fusion, the system knows whether you are a Requestor, Compliance Officer (Contributor), Approver, or Administrator.

docs.title: How to Log In
docs.text:
1. Open your web browser and go to the KYC system address (provided by IT)
  2. You will be redirected to the company's login page (the same page used for other systems)
  3. Enter your Fusion/network username and password
  4. The system opens directly on your personalised home page

docs.title: What You See Depends on Your Role
docs.text: Your Role What You See Where You Start Requestor (any QD employee) Intake portal only — submit requests, track your submissions Request Status page Contributor (Compliance Officer) Full KYC system — create entities, write reports, manage your queue My Worklist Approver L1 Approval queue — review and act on submitted reports Approval Queue Approver L2 / MLRO Final approval queue — high-stakes reviews with SAR gate L2 Approval Queue Administrator Everything above, plus user management and reference data Executive Dashboard

docs.title: For Requestors: Submitting a KYC Request
Step 1 — Open the Request Form
docs.text: From your home page, click "New KYC Request". The form opens with your name and department already filled in.

docs.title: Step 2 — Tell Us About the Counterparty
docs.text: Fill in the details of the person or company you want to do business with: - Their name and country - Whether they are an individual or a company - The type of relationship (supplier, buyer, tenant, etc.) - Whether there is any financial involvement - Whether there are any known connections to other QD relationships

docs.title: Step 3 — The System Checks Whether a KYC Is Needed
docs.text:
Based on your answers, the system automatically decides whether a full KYC report is required or whether a simplified evidence record is sufficient. This replaces the Excel calculator.

If KYC Not Required:
  → A waiver record is created automatically
  → Your documents are safely stored as evidence
  → You receive a confirmation

If KYC Required:
  → Continue to document upload

docs.title: Step 4 — Upload Your Documents
docs.text: The system shows you a checklist of which documents are needed based on the type of entity and their country. Upload each document and label its type (e.g., Commercial Registration, Passport, Ownership Declaration).

docs.title: Step 5 — Submit
docs.text: Click Submit. You will receive a confirmation with your unique case reference number (e.g., INTAKE-2025-000123).

docs.title: Tracking Your Request
docs.text:
Go to "My Requests" at any time to see the current status of all your submissions:

Status Meaning Pending Review Compliance team is reviewing your documents Documents Needed Compliance team has requested additional information In Progress Your KYC is being worked on Awaiting Approval Report is with the approver Approved KYC complete — you will receive the report by email Rejected KYC could not be approved — see the reason in the system

docs.title: For Compliance Officers: Your Daily Workflow
My Worklist
docs.text: When you log in, your Worklist shows everything that needs your attention, organised by priority: - New cases assigned to you - Reports you have drafted but not yet submitted - Reports that have been sent back to you with a request for more information (RFI) - SLA status: which reports are approaching or past their target completion date (green/amber/red)

docs.title: Creating an Entity
docs.text:
Before writing a KYC report, you record the counterparty as an Entity in the system.

Step 1: Duplicate Check Type the entity's name. The system searches existing records automatically and shows you similar names already in the system. If the same company exists, you can link to it rather than creating a duplicate.

Step 2: Fill in Entity Details The form adjusts based on whether the counterparty is an individual or a company. For companies, you also add the UBOs and authorised signatories.

Step 3: Record Screening Results After running WorldCheck (or your screening tool), come back to the system and complete the structured screening section: - When you screened them - Which database you used - Whether there was a match, and if so — genuine or false positive - Whether they are a PEP - Your findings in free text

Why this matters: These structured fields are what a regulator or auditor will look at if they examine your work. A free-text paragraph is harder to stand behind than a clear, structured record.

docs.title: Creating a KYC Report
docs.text:
Click New KYC Report and select the entity you just created. The system pre-fills everything it already knows from the entity record and the intake form — you will not be re-typing data you already entered.

What you fill in: - KYC Type (Simplified / AdHoc / Enhanced) - Risk Level — the system suggests one based on the entity's country and screening results. If you disagree, you can change it, but you must note why. - Conclusion — select a template from the dropdown, and the standard text appears in the conclusion field, ready for you to personalise - Next Steps

The form shows your SLA indicator: how many days have passed versus your target completion time. Green means on track. Amber means approaching the limit. Red means you are past it.

Save as Draft if you need to come back to it. Submit for Approval when the report is complete.

docs.title: Responding to an RFI
docs.text: When an approver sends a report back to you with a question: 1. You receive an email notification 2. Go to your Worklist — the report is there with a flag 3. Click the report, read the approver's comment in the History tab 4. Make the necessary changes or add a response in the comments section 5. Resubmit

docs.title: Your Approval Queue
docs.text: Your queue shows all reports waiting for your review. Each row shows: - Report reference and counterparty name - KYC type and risk level (colour-coded: red = high, amber = medium, green = low) - Who submitted it and when - Days pending versus SLA target

docs.title: Reviewing a Report
docs.text:
Click Review on any report. A review panel opens with four tabs:

Tab Content Summary All KYC fields, risk assessment, conclusion Entity & UBOs Entity details, UBO list, structured screening results per UBO Documents Attached files — click to view inline in the browser History Every action taken on this report, with dates, users, and comments

docs.title: Taking Action
docs.text:
After reviewing, scroll to the bottom of the panel:

Approve - For low-risk reports: this is the final approval — report is complete, requestor is notified automatically - For medium/high-risk: passes to the Level 2 queue

Request For Information (RFI) - Select the type of issue (Missing Document / Unclear Conclusion / Insufficient Screening / Other) - Enter your comment - Click Send — the report returns to the contributor with your question

Reject - Enter the reason (mandatory) - The report is closed and both the contributor and requestor are notified

docs.title: When You Are on Leave
docs.text: Go to your profile and mark yourself as On Leave. Your pre-configured deputy (set by your administrator) will automatically receive your tasks. When you return, unmark yourself — your queue resumes immediately.

docs.title: For Level 2 / MLRO Approvers
docs.text: The Level 2 process is the same as Level 1, with one additional step before you can approve:

docs.title: The SAR Gate
docs.text:
Before completing a final approval, you must answer:

"Based on your review of this report, does any information warrant a Suspicious Activity Report (SAR)?"

  • No → proceed to approve normally
  • Yes → the approval is paused; the Head of Compliance and system administrator are notified; the SAR process follows separately

This is not bureaucracy — it is a legal obligation. The system ensures it is never skipped.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
Go to Administration → User Management to see all users synchronised from Oracle Fusion. The system automatically imports all active employees. You can: - Override a user's KYC role if their Fusion job code does not map correctly - Set a deputy approver for each approver - Mark an approver as on leave (activates their deputy) - View the delegation log

Note: You do not create or delete users manually. The system syncs with Fusion nightly. New employees appear automatically; those who leave are deactivated automatically.

docs.title: Reference Data
docs.text:
All configurable lists are managed under Administration → Reference Data: - Business Counterparty Categories - Relationship Types - Conclusion Templates (by risk level) - Country Risk Tiers (FATF status) - Report Statuses

Changes take effect immediately for all new records.

docs.title: Monitoring Dashboard
docs.text:
The Executive Dashboard shows real-time KPIs:

Panel Shows Pipeline Summary What is currently in each stage Completed This Month Count + average days to complete SLA Compliance % of reports finished on time Risk Breakdown Low / Medium / High pie chart Overdue Cases past their SLA target Upcoming Reviews KYCs due for renewal in the next 60 days

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text:
Q: What if I submitted a request and need to add more documents? A: Go to My Requests, open the request, and use the "Add Document" button. Documents can be added at any stage before final approval.

Q: What if my approver is on holiday and no one is reviewing my report? A: The system handles this automatically. When an approver marks themselves on leave, their deputy receives the tasks. If you believe there is a routing problem, contact your compliance administrator.

Q: How do I know when my KYC request is complete? A: You will receive an email with the completed report attached. You can also check My Requests in the portal at any time.

Q: Can I edit a report after submitting it for approval? A: Not directly — once submitted, the report is in the approver's hands. If something needs to change, the approver can issue an RFI, which returns it to you for editing.

Q: How long is my session active? A: Your session expires after 30 minutes of inactivity. You will be redirected to the login page.

Q: What happens to old KYC records? A: All records are retained for at least 5 years after approval. They remain searchable and viewable throughout this period.

docs.title: 2.1 Core Tables (DDL Summary)

All tables follow these standards: - Primary key: NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY - Audit columns on every table: created_by, created_date, updated_by, updated_date, row_version - created_by defaults to SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER') - created_date defaults to SYSTIMESTAMP - Enum-style columns enforced via CHECK constraints (no lookup join needed for validation)

docs.title: 2.2 Audit Trigger Template
docs.text:
Apply to every table in the schema:

CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_<TABLE>_AUR
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON QD_KYC_<TABLE>
  FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  IF INSERTING THEN
    :NEW.created_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.created_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := 1;
  ELSIF UPDATING THEN
    :NEW.updated_by   := NVL(SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER'), USER);
    :NEW.updated_date := SYSTIMESTAMP;
    :NEW.row_version  := NVL(:OLD.row_version, 0) + 1;
  END IF;
END;

  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_ENTITY FOR EACH ROW

  :NEW.entity_ref := 'ENT-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_ENTITY_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');

CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER QD_KYC_REPORT_BIR
  BEFORE INSERT ON QD_KYC_REPORT FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  :NEW.report_ref := 'KYC-' || TO_CHAR(SYSDATE,'YYYY')
                     || '-' || LPAD(QD_KYC_REPORT_SEQ.NEXTVAL,6,'0');
  :NEW.due_diligence_type := CASE :NEW.kyc_type
    WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 'Simplified Due Diligence (SDD)'
    WHEN 'ENHANCED'   THEN 'Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)'
    ELSE 'Standard Due Diligence' END;
  :NEW.review_cycle_months := CASE :NEW.risk_level
    WHEN 'HIGH' THEN 12 WHEN 'MEDIUM' THEN 24 ELSE 36 END;
  :NEW.next_review_date := ADD_MONTHS(SYSDATE, :NEW.review_cycle_months);
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION QD_KYC_SECURITY.REPORT_POLICY(
  schema_name VARCHAR2, table_name VARCHAR2

  v_role    VARCHAR2(30) := SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_KYC_ROLE');
  v_uid     VARCHAR2(20) := SYS_CONTEXT('APEX$SESSION','APP_USER_ID');
BEGIN
  RETURN CASE v_role
    WHEN 'ADMIN'       THEN '1=1'
    WHEN 'APPROVER_L2' THEN '1=1'
    WHEN 'APPROVER_L1' THEN 'wf_level >= 1'
    WHEN 'CONTRIBUTOR' THEN

      ' OR report_id IN (SELECT report_id FROM QD_KYC_WF_COMMENTS ' ||
      'WHERE comment_type = ''RFI_REQUEST'')'
    ELSE '1=0'
  END;

Property Value Page Title KYC Approval Queue — Level 1 Authorization IS_APPROVER_L1 Source QD_KYC_V_APPROVAL_QUEUE_L1 (view joining report + user + intake)

View definition: 

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW QD_KYC_V_APPROVAL_QUEUE_L1 AS
SELECT
  r.report_id, r.report_ref, r.kyc_type, r.risk_level,
  r.report_status, r.submitted_date,
  ROUND(SYSDATE - r.submitted_date) AS days_pending,
  u.full_name AS contributor_name,
  e.entity_name,
  CASE r.kyc_type
    WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 5 WHEN 'ENHANCED' THEN 20 ELSE 10
  END AS sla_days,
  CASE
    WHEN ROUND(SYSDATE - r.submitted_date) > CASE r.kyc_type
      WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 5 WHEN 'ENHANCED' THEN 20 ELSE 10 END
    THEN 'OVERDUE' ELSE 'ON_TRACK'
  END AS sla_status
FROM QD_KYC_REPORT r
JOIN QD_KYC_USERS  u ON u.user_id = r.contributor_user_id
JOIN QD_KYC_ENTITY e ON e.entity_id = r.entity_id
WHERE r.report_status IN ('SUBMITTED','RFI_L1')
AND   r.wf_level = 1;

Row Highlight Rules (Interactive Report → Highlight): - Name: Overdue | Condition: SLA_STATUS = 'OVERDUE' | CSS: u-hot - Name: Near SLA | Condition: DAYS_PENDING > SLA_DAYS - 2 | CSS: u-warning

Approval Action Process: 

-- Called from modal dialog submit
DECLARE
  v_action VARCHAR2(20) := :P13_ACTION;  -- APPROVE / RFI / REJECT
BEGIN
  -- Write to process log (immutable)
  INSERT INTO QD_KYC_PROCESS_LOG (report_id, action_type, from_status, to_status, action_user_id, comments)
  VALUES (:P13_REPORT_ID, v_action,
          (SELECT report_status FROM QD_KYC_REPORT WHERE report_id = :P13_REPORT_ID),
          CASE v_action WHEN 'APPROVE' THEN 'APPROVED_L1'
                        WHEN 'RFI' THEN 'RFI_L1' ELSE 'REJECTED' END,
          :APP_USER_ID, :P13_COMMENT);

  -- Update report status
  UPDATE QD_KYC_REPORT SET
    report_status = CASE v_action WHEN 'APPROVE' THEN 'APPROVED_L1'
                                  WHEN 'RFI' THEN 'RFI_L1' ELSE 'REJECTED' END,
    l1_approval_date = CASE v_action WHEN 'APPROVE' THEN SYSTIMESTAMP END,
    wf_level = CASE v_action WHEN 'APPROVE' THEN 2 ELSE wf_level END
  WHERE report_id = :P13_REPORT_ID;

  -- Route by outcome
  CASE v_action
    WHEN 'APPROVE' THEN
      IF (SELECT risk_level FROM QD_KYC_REPORT WHERE report_id = :P13_REPORT_ID) = 'LOW' THEN
        QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.COMPLETE_FINAL(:P13_REPORT_ID);
      ELSE
        QD_KYC_NOTIFICATIONS.SEND_TO_ACTIVE_APPROVER('APPROVAL_REQUIRED_L2', :P13_REPORT_ID, 'APPROVER_L2');
      END IF;
    WHEN 'RFI' THEN
      INSERT INTO QD_KYC_WF_COMMENTS (report_id, comment_text, comment_type, posted_by_user_id, wf_status_at_time)
      VALUES (:P13_REPORT_ID, :P13_COMMENT, 'RFI_REQUEST', :APP_USER_ID, 'RFI_L1');
      QD_KYC_NOTIFICATIONS.SEND('RFI_ISSUED',
        (SELECT contributor_user_id FROM QD_KYC_REPORT WHERE report_id = :P13_REPORT_ID),
        :P13_REPORT_ID);
    WHEN 'REJECT' THEN
      QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.COMPLETE_REJECTED(:P13_REPORT_ID, :P13_COMMENT);
  END CASE;
END;

docs.title: 7.1 Workflow Activities (APEX Workflow Builder)
docs.text:
Workflow Name: KYC_APPROVAL_WORKFLOW
Version: 1.0

Activities:
1. DOCS_VALIDATION
   Type: Human Task
   Potential Owner: ROLE:COMPLIANCE_TEAM
   Due Days: 2
   Outcomes: DOCS_COMPLETE | DOCS_INCOMPLETE

2. ASSIGNMENT
   Type: Script Task
   Script: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.AUTO_ASSIGN(:INTAKE_ID)
   Outcomes: ASSIGNED

3. DUE_DILIGENCE
   Type: Human Task
   Potential Owner: ASSIGNED_USER (from workflow variable)
   Due Days: Computed from KYC type (5/10/20)
   Outcomes: SUBMITTED_FOR_APPROVAL | SAVE_DRAFT

4. RISK_GATEWAY
   Type: Exclusive Gateway
   Condition LOW:  risk_level = 'LOW'  → L1_APPROVAL
   Condition ELSE: risk_level != 'LOW' → L1_APPROVAL → L2_APPROVAL

5. L1_APPROVAL
   Type: Human Task
   Potential Owner: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.GET_ACTIVE_APPROVER('APPROVER_L1')
   Due Days: 3
   Outcomes: APPROVED_L1 | RFI_L1 | REJECTED_L1
   On RFI: loop back to DUE_DILIGENCE

6. L2_APPROVAL
   Type: Human Task
   Potential Owner: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.GET_ACTIVE_APPROVER('APPROVER_L2')
   Due Days: 3
   Outcomes: APPROVED_FINAL | RFI_L2 | REJECTED_L2 | SAR_FLAGGED

7. FINAL_COMPLETE
   Type: Script Task
   Script: QD_KYC_WORKFLOW.COMPLETE_FINAL(:REPORT_ID)

8. SAR_REVIEW (conditional branch)
   Type: Human Task — MLRO only
   Outcomes: SAR_FILED | SAR_DISMISSED
   On DISMISSED: return to L2_APPROVAL

docs.text:
-- Full nightly job covering monitoring, SLA alerts, and Fusion sync
BEGIN
  DBMS_SCHEDULER.CREATE_JOB(
    job_name        => 'QD_KYC_NIGHTLY_JOB',
    job_type        => 'PLSQL_BLOCK',
    job_action      => Q'[
      DECLARE
        CURSOR c_review_due IS
          SELECT report_id, contributor_user_id
          FROM   QD_KYC_REPORT
          WHERE  next_review_date BETWEEN SYSDATE AND SYSDATE + 60
          AND    report_status = 'APPROVED';

        CURSOR c_overdue IS
          SELECT report_id, contributor_user_id
          FROM   QD_KYC_REPORT
          WHERE  next_review_date < SYSDATE
          AND    report_status = 'APPROVED';

        CURSOR c_sla_breach IS
          SELECT r.report_id
          FROM   QD_KYC_REPORT r
          WHERE  r.report_status NOT IN ('APPROVED','REJECTED','DRAFT')
          AND    r.submitted_date IS NOT NULL
          AND    SYSDATE - r.submitted_date >
                 CASE r.kyc_type WHEN 'SIMPLIFIED' THEN 5
                                 WHEN 'ENHANCED' THEN 20 ELSE 10 END;
      BEGIN
        FOR r IN c_review_due LOOP
          QD_KYC_NOTIFICATIONS.SEND('REVIEW_DUE_SOON', r.contributor_user_id, r.report_id);
        END LOOP;
        FOR r IN c_overdue LOOP
          QD_KYC_NOTIFICATIONS.SEND('REVIEW_OVERDUE', r.contributor_user_id, r.report_id);
        END LOOP;
        FOR r IN c_sla_breach LOOP
          QD_KYC_NOTIFICATIONS.SEND_ADMIN_ALERT('SLA breach on report_id=' || r.report_id);
        END LOOP;
        QD_KYC_FUSION_SYNC.SYNC_ALL_EMPLOYEES;
        APEX_MAIL.PUSH_QUEUE;
      END;]',
    start_date      => TRUNC(SYSDATE+1) + 6/24,
    repeat_interval => 'FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=6;BYMINUTE=0',
    enabled         => TRUE
  );

docs.text:
Document Purpose

Plain-language overview of the current KYC application (built on JavaServer Faces) — what it does, how it works, and what its limitations are.

docs.title: Current KYC Management Application
docs.text: Document Type: Business Overview Audience: Compliance Team, Management, Business Stakeholders System: Existing JSF Web Application Status: Live Production System

docs.title: What Is This System?
docs.text:
The KYC Management Application is Qatari Diar's internal web-based system for managing Know Your Customer (KYC) due diligence reports. It replaces paper files and email chains with a digital record of every counterparty screened by the Enterprise Risk & Compliance team.

A counterparty is any person or company that Qatari Diar plans to do business with — a supplier, buyer, tenant, contractor, investor, or joint venture partner.

Before QD enters into a significant business relationship, the compliance team must research the counterparty, verify their identity, assess any risks, and obtain management approval. This system manages that process from start to finish.

docs.title: Who Uses It?
docs.text: Role What They Do in the System Contributor Compliance officer who creates and submits KYC reports Level 1 Approver Reviews and approves reports for low-risk cases; first reviewer for medium/high risk Level 2 / RFI Approver Final sign-off for medium and high-risk cases; handles information requests Administrator Manages users, reference data, and system configuration

docs.title: 1. Manages Counterparty Records (Entities)
docs.text:
Before creating a KYC report, the compliance team records information about the counterparty in the system. This is called an Entity.

For a natural person (an individual), the system captures: - Full name, nationality, date of birth - ID or passport number - Screening results from international databases

For a legal entity (a company), the system captures: - Company name, registration number, headquarters - Ownership structure - Details of the people who ultimately own or control the company — these are called Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs)

Each UBO's identity is recorded individually, including their nationality, ID number, and the results of screening them through international databases.

docs.title: 2. Creates and Manages KYC Reports
docs.text:
A KYC report is the formal compliance document that records everything the team has found about a counterparty and what decision was reached.

Each report includes: - Which company or person was investigated - What type of relationship QD plans to have with them - What level of due diligence was applied (Simplified, Standard, or Enhanced) - What the screening found - The compliance officer's conclusion and recommendation - The assessed risk level (Low, Medium, or High) - Supporting documents

docs.title: 3. Routes Reports Through an Approval Process
docs.text:
Once a compliance officer completes a report, it goes through a formal approval process before it is finalised.

flowchart TD
    CO([Compliance Officer\nCreates Report]) --> SUBMIT[Submits for Approval]
    SUBMIT --> L1[Level 1 Approver\nReviews]
    L1 --> A1{Decision}
    A1 -->|Approve — Low Risk| FINAL([✅ Final Approval])
    A1 -->|Request More Info| RFI[Report returned\nto Officer with comment]
    A1 -->|Reject| REJ1([❌ Closed])
    RFI --> RESUBMIT[Officer responds\nand resubmits]
    RESUBMIT --> L1
    A1 -->|Approve — Medium/High Risk| L2[Level 2 Approver\nReviews]
    L2 --> A2{Decision}
    A2 -->|Final Approve| FINAL
    A2 -->|Request More Info| RFI
    A2 -->|Reject| REJ2([❌ Closed])

    style FINAL fill:#E8F5E9,color:#1B5E20,stroke:#2E7D32
    style REJ1 fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style REJ2 fill:#FFEBEE,color:#7F0000,stroke:#B71C1C
    style RFI fill:#FFF3E0,color:#BF360C,stroke:#E65100

Important rule: A report cannot be approved by the same person who created it. Low-risk reports require one approval signature. Medium and high-risk reports require two separate approvals.

docs.title: 4. Tracks Everything with a Full Audit Trail
docs.text: Every action taken — every submission, approval, rejection, or request for information — is permanently recorded with the date, time, and the name of the person who took the action. This audit trail cannot be edited or deleted.

docs.title: 5. Stores Supporting Documents
docs.text: The system holds all documents submitted as evidence: commercial registrations, identity documents, shareholder certificates, and any other supporting material. These documents are linked directly to the KYC report they support.

docs.title: 6. Generates PDF Reports
docs.text: The system can produce a formal PDF version of any KYC report. Unfinished reports are watermarked as "Draft" to prevent them from being used as official documents.

docs.title: 7. Provides Search and Filtering
docs.text: The compliance team can search the full history of KYC reports by: - Reference number - Counterparty name - Risk level (Low / Medium / High) - Approval status - Report status - The officer who conducted the due diligence

docs.title: How a KYC Report Moves Through the System
Step-by-Step
docs.text:
Step 1 — Create the Entity The compliance officer creates a record for the counterparty, entering their details and the results of searching them against international screening databases (WorldCheck and others).

Step 2 — Add UBOs (if a company) If the counterparty is a company, the officer records each significant owner or authorised signatory — including their screening results.

Step 3 — Create the KYC Report The officer creates the formal report, linking it to the entity, classifying the type of due diligence, recording the findings and conclusion, setting the risk level, and attaching supporting documents.

Step 4 — Save as Draft or Submit The officer can save a draft to complete later, or submit the finished report for approval.

Step 5 — Level 1 Review The appointed Level 1 Approver reviews the full report, including all documents. They can approve it, send it back with questions, or reject it.

Step 6 — Level 2 Review (Medium/High Risk) For anything above low risk, a second senior approver independently reviews and makes the final decision.

Step 7 — Completion Once fully approved, the report is finalised and archived. A PDF can be generated and sent to the team that originally requested the KYC.

docs.title: Reference Data the System Manages
docs.text:
The system uses configurable reference tables that administrators can update without changing the software:

  • Business Counterparty Categories — e.g., Supplier, Buyer, Investor, Tenant
  • Report Statuses — with colour codes for quick visual identification
  • Screening Results — categories for what the international databases returned
  • Request Originators — the teams or individuals who requested KYC checks

docs.title: What the System Does Not Currently Do
docs.text:
Being transparent about current limitations helps set expectations:

Limitation Impact No automatic notification to the original requester when a report is approved Requesters must be informed manually No live KPI dashboard — metrics require a manual data export Management reporting is slow and labour-intensive No scheduled reminders for periodic KYC reviews Overdue reviews are not flagged automatically No digital intake from requesting departments — requests arrive by email Inconsistent formats, no tracking Passwords are not strongly secured Security risk that should be addressed

These limitations are addressed in Version 3 (Best Practice) and Version 4 (APEX Implementation).

docs.title: Key Terms
docs.text: Term Meaning KYC Know Your Customer — the process of verifying who a counterparty is and assessing their risk Counterparty Any person or company QD does business with Entity The system record for a counterparty UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner — the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a legal entity Due Diligence The investigation and research process SDD Simplified Due Diligence — applied to low-risk cases EDD Enhanced Due Diligence — applied to high-risk cases PEP Politically Exposed Person — someone in a prominent public position Workflow Status Where a report currently sits in the approval process Process Reference The unique ID number assigned to each KYC report Audit Trail The permanent, tamper-proof record of every action

docs.text:
Document Purpose

How the KYC process works today — documented from the requirements gathering session. Eight phases, from Excel calculator to manual PDF reports. Includes 16 identified pain points.

docs.title: How We Work Today: The As-Is KYC Process
docs.text:
Document Type: Business Process Guide Audience: Compliance Team, Management Source: Requirements Gathering Session — Head of Enterprise Risk & Compliance Status: Current manual process — basis for all future improvements

This document faithfully captures how the compliance team currently operates — including every manual step, every tool used, and every known difficulty. It is not a criticism; it is an honest baseline from which to improve.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Today, the KYC process at Qatari Diar is a mostly manual process. The existing KYC Report Application (a JSF-based web system) is used only at the end: the officer enters the completed report data and the system manages the approval workflow and record storage. Everything before that — receiving requests, collecting documents, conducting due diligence, and compiling the full report — is done entirely outside the system through email, Excel, WorldCheck, and personal judgment. The system never sees the work; it only sees the finished output.

This creates real risks: inconsistency between departments, reliance on personal memory, difficulty onboarding new staff, and no reliable way to answer basic management questions like "how many KYC reports did we complete this quarter?" without first requesting a data export.

The process only enters the KYC Report Application once all manual work is complete — documents validated, due diligence researched, entity data ready. Everything before that point is invisible to the system.
